pure-announcement.rationale: This is a step-by-step implementation tutorial with code and a limitations analysis, not a launch, release note, or funding announcement.

duplicate.rationale: None of the nearest concepts (SLO burn-rate alerting, Agent Skills, context layer, eval notes) covers putting an LLM triage agent between anomaly detection and data-correcting action.

unfalsifiable.rationale: The full implementation is published on GitHub against a public API (disease.sh), so every claim about the system's behavior is reproducible.

durability.rationale: The transferable pattern — severity-gated agent triage where only minor anomalies are auto-fixed and criticals escalate to humans — is thin relative to the bulk of the note, which is a stack-specific walkthrough (phidata, GroqCloud, gpt-oss-120b, Streamlit) that will rot quickly.

actionability.rationale: A reader gets a complete runnable implementation plus explicit build guardrails: gate auto-correction by severity, never auto-fix critical anomalies, and never deploy the agent where anomalies trigger irreversible actions.

atomicity.rationale: The whole tutorial elaborates one statable idea: insert an LLM agent between statistical detection and downstream action to decide fix, keep, or escalate under severity constraints.
